target_customer: Gene therapy and cell therapy developers and manufacturers that need high yield viral vector production
problem: Viral vector manufacturing is a bottleneck for gene therapies; yield is low and each therapeutic needs its own producer cell line.
business_model: Platform and product company selling engineered cell lines and production technologies, plus partnerships
product_category: Biotech tools, cell line engineering for viral vectors

founders.name: Lexi Rovner
prior_employers: Harvard Medical School (postdoc in George Church's lab)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Honors: Endpoints 20 under 40 (2022).

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping millions of cell genotypes to vector production phenotypes with DNA library synthesis, sequencing and computation is research grade biotech.

defensibility.rationale: A Harvard and Wyss spinout with a screening platform and a growing CellMap dataset; hard for a small team to replicate.

incumbents: Large CDMOs and cell line vendors
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; the company raised a $55M Series A in 2022 and launched product lines afterward.

market_need_then: Gene therapy interest was exploding by 2018 and a 2018 review (Smith, Grieger and Samulski) warned that manufacturing bottlenecks must be addressed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific, aimed at next generation medicines.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in biotech trade press after its 2020 and 2022 announcements; no brand story or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: 64x Bio built a viral vector cell line platform out of Harvard and Wyss research, stayed in stealth until 2020, and then raised a 4.5 million dollar seed and a 55 million dollar Series A in 2022. It is active and expanding product lines, with scientific credibility and a real manufacturing bottleneck as its drivers.
notes: The seed date and amount come from search snippets of the BusinessWire release (page returned 403); CB Insights also lists a seed dated 2018-07 and startupintros says $5M, unresolved. Founding year conflict: YC 2017, others 2018. One source calls the CEO Alex Rovner; YC says Lexi. No dated competitor source found for 2018 (searches returned later reviews and the 2018 review article only), so competitors are empty.
